South Dakota.available: very limited — no general expungement of adult convictions
South Dakota.waiting_period: 1 year after dismissal or no-charge arrest; automatic removal of minor offenses after about 5–10 years (sources vary)
South Dakota.what_qualifies: arrests never charged, dismissed charges, acquittals; petty/Class 2 misdemeanor offenses auto-removed after about 10 years

Tennessee.filing_fee: varies by county, roughly $120–$275 including service
Tennessee.waiting_period: none for dismissals/acquittals; 5 years after sentence completion for misdemeanors and Class E felonies, 10 years for eligible Class C/D and drug felonies
Tennessee.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted charges; eligible nonviolent misdemeanors and certain Class C–E felonies

Texas.filing_fee: varies by county, typically $35–$60 filing (service extra)
Texas.waiting_period: none for acquittals; 180 days–3 years by offense level for dismissals; 5 years after discharge for most felony nondisclosures
Texas.what_qualifies: acquitted or dismissed charges, pardons; deferred-adjudication cases get nondisclosure (sealing)

Utah.waiting_period: 3–10 years depending on offense class (3 yrs Class C misdemeanor, 4 yrs Class B, 5 yrs Class A/felony drug possession, 7 yrs most felonies, 10 yrs DUI)
Utah.what_qualifies: arrests without conviction; eligible misdemeanors and some nonviolent felonies within conviction-count limits

Vermont.max_claim: $10,000 ($5,000 for consumer credit and medical debt claims)
Vermont.waiting_period: 5 years after sentence completion for expungement; dismissed charges auto-sealed after about 60 days
Vermont.what_qualifies: qualifying nonviolent misdemeanors and some nonviolent felonies; dismissed charges sealed automatically

Virginia.available: yes — expungement for non-convictions, sealing for some convictions since 2025
Virginia.lawyer_allowed: generally no — self-represented (case moves to the regular docket if a lawyer appears)
Virginia.max_claim: $5,000 (small claims division of General District Court)
Virginia.waiting_period: none for dismissals/acquittals; 7 crime-free years for automatic sealing of eligible misdemeanors, 10 years for eligible felonies
Virginia.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted charges; since July 2025, certain misdemeanor and Class 5/6 felony convictions

Washington.lawyer_allowed: no, unless the judge gives permission
Washington.waiting_period: 3 years after sentence completion (misdemeanors), 5 years (Class C felonies), 10 years (Class B felonies)
Washington.what_qualifies: certain misdemeanors and Class B/C felonies; not DUI or most sex/violent offenses

West Virginia.available: yes — expungement of misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies
West Virginia.waiting_period: 1 year (single misdemeanor), 2 years (multiple misdemeanors), 5 years (nonviolent felony) after sentence/supervision ends
West Virginia.what_qualifies: misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies from the same transaction; excludes violent, sexual, DUI, and domestic-violence offenses

Wisconsin.waiting_period: no fixed waiting period — ordered at sentencing and takes effect after sentence completion
Wisconsin.what_qualifies: under 25 at the time of the offense, offense carries 6 years or less maximum imprisonment, ordered at sentencing

Wyoming.waiting_period: 180 days for arrest records; 5 years for misdemeanors; 10 years for felonies after sentence completion
Wyoming.what_qualifies: arrests never charged, dismissed charges, acquittals; eligible misdemeanor and nonviolent felony convictions
